howWeMakeVideos.title: How we make videos (one screen)
howWeMakeVideos.intro: Every video shows the real product. Higgsfield adds short cinematic scenes around it: an opening shot, a moment in the middle, the scene behind the end card, or a slow camera move over a real result. HyperFrames puts every word, timer and the brand on top. Nothing generated is ever shown as Makeborne itself.

ways.name: 1. Record the screen, add the words
ways.covers: Speedruns, demos, tutorials, before and after, 'made from one sentence'
steps: Type one sentence into Makeborne and record the screen while it builds. Never stop the recording.
Record one change in chat, then publish or export.
Open the matching template, drop the recording in, type the words that appear on screen.
If you sped the build up, the little clock says so ('Sped up ×8').
Record your voice over it, add captions, check it on your phone, post.
ways.time: About 2 hours the first time, 1.5 hours after that

ways.name: 2. Talk to the phone
ways.covers: Day 1, Day 7, Day 30, 'why no free plan', 'who's behind this'
steps: Phone at eye level, window light, say the five lines. Three takes.
Keep the best take, cut the pauses.
Add the 'Day N' tag, the real numbers (typed from Whop, never rounded up) and captions.
Show screen clips in the bottom half only, never over your face.
LinkedIn gets the captioned version without music.

ways.name: 3. Picture posts
ways.covers: Statics, carousels, stories, X cards, link previews
steps: Take a screenshot of a real Makeborne result.
Open the picture template, paste the exact headline from the plan.
One coloured italic word, the price and the refund line at the bottom.
Save one image per page, check it at phone size.
Post, or join the pages into a PDF for LinkedIn.
ways.time: About 25-45 minutes, 1.5-2 hours for a carousel

ways.name: 4. Add a Higgsfield scene
ways.share: 15 videos now, 5 more when their feature is live; 1-4 scenes each
ways.covers: Opening shots (the café at dawn, the pitch room, the bookshelf), a moment in the middle, the end card over a scene, a slow camera move over a real result, Black Friday and the holidays
steps: Open the shot card in Library › Production and copy the prompt. Upload only what the card says: never unfinished features, client work or customer data.
In Higgsfield pick the model and camera move on the card: 9:16, 1080p. Make the takes it says (usually 3).
Keep the first good take: no people, no letters, nothing that looks like our app. Save it with its prompt and seed.
Drop it into the HyperFrames slot the sheet names (opening, middle, end) and type the words in HyperFrames.
The 'AI-generated scene' label stays on for every second of the scene. Switch on the platform's AI label when you post.
ways.time: About 10 minutes per shot in Higgsfield, plus 20-30 minutes per video in HyperFrames

howWeMakeVideos.everythingElse: The rest is creators (they film themselves, we check the draft) and the two brand films. Founder, creator, tutorial and proof videos stay real-only on purpose.
rules: Only show what is live today.
No fake customers, ever: no AI people at all.
Every sped-up build says so on screen.
Every Higgsfield second carries the 'AI-generated scene' label, and nothing generated looks like our app.
howWeMakeVideos.budget: Higgsfield Plus, $49 for the first month, bought by the owner himself. It is separate from the $1,000 ads budget and never mixed with it.
howWeMakeVideos.mix: In a video with Higgsfield: about two thirds real product, a quarter Higgsfield scenes, the rest HyperFrames cards. Every word is HyperFrames.

stack.why: The product is the proof, so real captures carry every video. Higgsfield adds the cinematic seconds a screen recording cannot (the shop at dawn, the pitch room, the bookshelf, the seasonal beats), labelled and never showing product UI. HyperFrames sets every word, timer and the brand exactly and assembles the clips with the real captures. The founder's face carries trust.
stack.recommendation: HyperFrames + real captures as the base ($0/month) plus Higgsfield Plus monthly ($49, production budget, owner signs up Tue 27 Oct). Keep, downgrade to Starter or cancel at the Sun 22 Nov review by the measured lift.

captureStandards.account: A clean owner account on production makeborne.com used only for marketing: fictional display name, no real e-mail visible, an empty bookmarks bar, a dedicated browser profile, no other tabs. Crop out the account e-mail, avatar, browser tabs and bookmarks. Never show a Whop store page or any unreleased menu item.
captureStandards.desktop: OBS, 60 fps, CQP/CRF high quality. Two window sizes: 1440x900 CSS px at 2x device scale (records 2880x1800) for 16:9 and punch-ins, and 860x1080 CSS px at 2x (records 1720x2160) for vertical-first composer shots. Browser zoom 100%; the 2x comes from the display scale so text is sharp when punched in. Cursor highlight on; system notifications off.
captureStandards.phone: Native screen recording at 60 fps, Do Not Disturb on, battery and time not distracting. For a physical phone in frame: a second phone on a tripod at eye level, window light, no hand blur.
captureStandards.builds: Record every build uncut from Create to finished, and log brief, start and end time (m:ss) and credits in the run log. The uncut file is kept for the 90-150 s full cut, the landing page and the 'uncut build' DM reply. Punch cuts use data-playback-rate and the clock chip states the factor.
captureStandards.names: Every business name a build invents is checked against real trademarks and local businesses before it appears in a public frame (trademark office search plus a web search). Known traps: Tern, Tidal, 'Northface Labs', Galerie Nord, Kazu, Round Nine, Salt & Swell, Petal & Stem.
captureStandards.data: No personal data on screen: blur (12 px Gaussian in HyperFrames, or `npx hyperframes media-treatment`) every real business name, address, phone and e-mail in lead-finder results; crop Whop screens to totals only; handles blurred unless the person agreed.
captureStandards.reencode: Before editing: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -g 60 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an out.mp4` (keyframe every second at 60 fps; seeking never freezes).
captureStandards.storage: Captures go to the private asset library on a local disk, never into this public repository (production/.gitignore blocks media).

disclosure.summary: Real screen captures of our own product, the founder filming himself and typeset HTML need no AI label. Labels are required for (1) every Higgsfield second ('AI-generated scene' on screen plus the platform label), (2) image-to-video camera moves over real outputs ('AI camera move on a real Makeborne output'), (3) concept art shown in films, (4) generated images inside outputs after the images beat, and (5) every paid creator post. A fake customer testimonial by an AI avatar is never allowed.

byPlatform.rule: Turn on the AI-generated content label for any post with a realistic generated scene or person (Community Guidelines effective 24 Sep 2026). Brand account uses the Commercial Music Library only. Paid creators: branded-content toggle plus 'Ad' in video.

Meta adds 'AI info' automatically for content made with its own generative tools or detected through industry signals (C2PA); it appears under 'About this ad'. Use Meta's AI label on organic posts with realistic generated shots. Paid creators: paid-partnership label.

Altered or synthetic content = Yes for photorealistic generated scenes; not needed for captions, upscaling, AI-written scripts, our own real captures or a non-realistic stylised plate. Label shows on the player for photorealistic content.

From 2 Aug 2026: a generated image or video that resembles real people, places or events and could falsely appear authentic is a deepfake: label it clearly at first exposure (the final Code of Practice of 10 Jun 2026 points to an EU icon or equivalent label). Evidently artistic or fictional shots get a lighter disclosure. Makeborne as a provider must also mark its own generated images machine-readably once images ship (gate box 6).

Testimonials must come from real people with real experience; AI-generated reviewers and fake customers are banned (16 CFR 465), and the ASA applies its testimonial rules to deepfakes and synthetic people. Creator posts disclose the material connection in the video itself. Credits for sharing reward the act of sharing, never positive sentiment.

realVsAiBroll.finding: No controlled public study compares screen-recorded demos with AI b-roll for SaaS conversion (searched 26 Oct 2026). The evidence that exists points one way: conversion content in this category shows the UI, the finished artifact and a next step (LightReel, Oct 2026); text-plus-product statics lead Meta hit rates (Motion 2026); fully AI-made ads underperform human-made versions of the same briefs on sales impact (Ipsos/Syracuse, May 2026); and AI tells (uncanny visuals, fast montages that hide flaws) trigger backlash (NN/G, Dec 2025).
realVsAiBroll.recommendation: In a video with Higgsfield: about 60-70% real product footage, 20-30% labelled Higgsfield scenes (hooks, mood, transitions, seasonal beats, camera moves over real outputs) and all text, timing and brand in HyperFrames. Founder, creator, tutorial and proof videos stay real-only. Never product proof from a generator. Judge on /go/ clicks and sales per 1,000 views and move the mix weekly.

higgsfield.everyShot: 9:16, 1080p, no generated audio (music comes from the platform libraries). Copy the prompt and the negative exactly. hardRules: Never generate fake product UI or fake outputs and present them as real. Every app screen and every output on screen is a real capture; a generated clip never shows a screen with content.

Never an AI avatar or any synthetic person as a 'customer', user or creator, and no testimonial of any kind from a generated person (FTC 16 CFR 465; the ASA applies its testimonial rules to synthetic people). In practice: no people at all in our generations.

An on-screen label on every generated second ('AI-generated scene'; 'AI camera move on a real Makeborne output' for image-to-video), plus the platform AI labels (TikTok AI-generated content, YouTube altered or synthetic, Meta AI label) and the EU AI Act Art. 50 first-exposure disclosure.

Never upload unreleased UI, client material, customer data or creator footage to Higgsfield: its standard terms allow training on inputs and outputs. The only uploads are image-to-video start frames that are outputs of live features made on the clean marketing account for the video itself (published sites, exported slides and book pages with fictional, trademark-checked names): material that is about to be posted anyway.
Only live features are shown as live. Shots for beat videos (V51, V55, V56, V58) are generated only after their feature passes the six-box gate.

mix.target: In a video with Higgsfield: about 60-70% real product footage, 20-30% Higgsfield scenes, the rest HyperFrames-only cards; every letter, timer and the brand is HyperFrames, over everything.

measured.wholePlanNote: Across all 60 videos (3023 s, including the founder, creator, tutorial and proof videos that stay real-only on purpose) Higgsfield is about 3.6% of posted seconds.

why: Real product footage is the proof and what converts in this category: the visible UI, the finished output and a next step (LightReel, Oct 2026); text-plus-product statics lead Meta hit rates (Motion 2026). So it stays the majority of every video (60-70%).

Higgsfield buys the first seconds and the feeling that screen recordings lack: the café at dawn, the empty pitch room, the bookshelf. That is where scroll-stopping happens, so it gets a real share (20-30%), not a token 2 s.

It stays capped: fully AI-made ads did worse on sales impact than human-made ones (Ipsos and Syracuse, May 2026) and visible AI tells cause backlash (NN/G, Dec 2025). Above about 30% the product stops being the star.
All text, timing and the brand are HyperFrames because generated video cannot be trusted with letters, and the timers ('Real time · m:ss', 'Sped up ×N') and prices must be exact.
The founder, creator, tutorial and proof videos stay real-only: trust there comes from a real face, real numbers and an uncut capture.

abTests.metric: /go/ link clicks per 1,000 views and tracked sales per 1,000 views, each version's first 7 days, same surface. Never views alone.
abTests.weeklyShift: Every Sunday: if the Higgsfield side of a pair (or the Higgsfield videos as a group) is 20%+ better on clicks per 1,000 views with sales per 1,000 views not lower, next week's new videos move 5 points toward Higgsfield (up to 30% of seconds); if 20%+ worse, 5 points back toward real (down to real-only); otherwise hold.
abTests.caveat: Organic posts on different days are not a controlled test: treat one pair as directional, three pairs pointing the same way as a decision.
